extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism ontology record bounded to claims directly supported by XML text, figures, and Table 3.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: D-alanylation of lipoteichoic acids increases GBS resistance to a subset of cationic antimicrobial peptides, especially natural linear/cyclic CAMPs, as shown by MIC90 comparisons between WT and ΔdltA strains.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: GBS NEM316 WT and isogenic cell-surface mutants exposed to Table 2 CAMP panel

source_locator.primary_source_statement: Table 2 reports MIC90 values for WT and mutant GBS strains.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Table 2 is phenotypic resistance evidence; it does not by itself prove the physical cell-wall mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper supports a cell-wall density/rigidity mechanism: TEM and AFM evidence show D-alanylated WT cell walls are denser/rigid relative to ΔdltA, with complementation restoring rigidity toward WT behavior.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: GBS cell wall in WT, ΔdltA, and complemented strains

source_locator.primary_source_statement: Figures 4 and 6 report cell-wall density and AFM rigidity evidence.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact image-derived measurements are not re-quantified from figures beyond the values and statistics reported by the article text/figure captions.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper supports reduced CAMP penetration through the D-alanylated GBS cell wall, using fluorescent peptide interaction experiments and Table 3 signal-change measurements.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: NBD/rhodamine-labeled LL37, magainin 2, and K5L7 interactions with intact GBS

source_locator.primary_source_statement: Table 3 and Figure 7 report fluorescence signal changes after peptide-bacteria interaction.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism is bounded to cell-wall penetration/rigidity evidence; it is not generalized to unrelated AMP mechanisms or direct peptide-target binding.
